rationale: This is a pure recombination of three already-evaluated archive legs (gross-margin windfall, industry-demeaned own-norm capex restraint, sales-growth MIN screen) with no new economic content, and stacking the three best-performing components in a strict triple conjunction mostly selects on prior in-sample noise while shrinking the effective long portfolio.

A legitimate but modest horizon variant of the archive winner `own_norm_profit_up_capex_down` — the 3y-vs-5y MA crossover genuinely separates regime shifts from project lumpiness, though the two windows overlap heavily so the test has less discriminating power than claimed and the profitability leg is left unchanged.

Well-constructed and internally consistent — both legs are same-unit asset-scaled own-norm deviations so the subtraction is economically meaningful (essentially the own-norm deviation in EBITDA-minus-capex per asset), and testing magnitude against the family's ubiquitous rank-product form answers a structural question the archive cannot; the main risk is that un-ranked raw deviations leave the FMB slope outlier-sensitive despite winsorization.

The "profit windfall" leg is not a profitability measure at all — (oancf − ib)/at is negative total accruals, so the signal rewards firms whose *earnings fall relative to cash flow*, which both contradicts the stated hypothesis of a cash-backed profit improvement and largely rediscovers the Sloan accruals anomaly in change form.

A coherent moderation hypothesis that is deliberately informative against `asset_light_margin_rents`, but multiplying by a strictly positive rank imposes a standalone monotone tilt toward capital-intensive firms rather than a clean interaction test, so a positive or negative result will be hard to attribute to moderation versus the level effect of asset heaviness.

A defensible dynamic recasting of the archive's high-slope R&D-mix signal, but the ratio's denominator means a rising xrd/(capx+xrd) deviation can be driven purely by falling capex — partially re-encoding the restraint leg rather than isolating a reallocation-toward-innovation decision — and xrd coverage near 0.07 will limit portfolio reliability.
